A-not-now.note: Rule 3 decides it: record only, no automatic follow-up.

A-stalled.note: Rule 6 decides it. Whether a draft is also acceptable is not addressed by the policy, so it stays allowed (as in v3).

T-ambig-existing-customer.note: Rules 5 and 8. Note: the support routing itself is a known gap, not built.

Q-lowconf-region.note: The region-handling part is decided by the policy (flag, never reject). The reviewer's separate view that the route should be 'qualified' is not decided by any policy, so band/route stay open (any band, route 'either').

T-inj-system-notice.note: Spam and unclear are both held for human review (rules 7 and 8), so the policy makes them operationally identical; it does not choose a primary label.

T-ambig-subcontract.note: The policy says unclear intent needs human review; it does not say whether a subcontracting request is 'genuine', 'unclear' or 'vendor'.

Q-ambig-brochure.note: No policy rule says whether a 'just browsing' request from a large company is nurture or qualified.

Q-ambig-vague.note: As above: the policy is silent on vague, low-intent enquiries.

Q-inj-research.note: No policy rule addresses an injected research note; both labellers agree 'high' is indefensible, and the rest is judgement.

changes.why_unambiguous: Policy: record the objection and timing context. 'no_action' alone does not record anything; a human task is allowed.
Policy: no automatic follow-up unless an approved policy permits it. No such policy exists, so no draft. (The reviewer's 'draft is acceptable' is superseded.)
Policy: flag for human review. flag_risk, a human-touch recommendation or a task all do that.
Policy: flag, and do not change the opportunity stage automatically. no_action ignores the stall; propose_field_change would change the deal.

A billing query is a support issue, not a sales enquiry: it must not enter automatic sales qualification. The system has no 'support' class (not built); 'unclear' is the only label that holds it for human review. 'genuine' would send it to qualification, contrary to the policy.

changes.v3: Not a sales enquiry; a good system routes to support/finance (out of scope).
changes.v4: A billing/support query. Policy rule 5 says route to the support or customer-success owner; that routing is NOT implemented (no support class exists). 'unclear' (held for human review, rule 8) is the only acceptable label.

changes.why_unambiguous: Region NA at confidence 0.25 must not disqualify and must be flagged for human verification.

Policy: route to a human sales representative. A task for the owner or a human-touch recommendation does that; a draft alone does not route to a human. (Supersedes the reviewer-adopted v3 list; a draft stays allowed in addition.)

Policy: stop promotional outreach immediately, but a marketing opt-out is not permission to ignore service obligations. Human tasks and human-touch recommendations are therefore NOT forbidden (v3 forbade them after the reviewer's suggestion); drafts, which in this system are promotional/sales replies, stay forbidden.

changes.v3: After a booked meeting the useful action is preparation, not more outreach.
changes.v4: Policy rule 4: meeting request -> prioritise human sales follow-up. Required: recommend_human_touch or recommend_task.
